t: Colchis exported gold, iron, timber and honey mostly to the Greek city-states, and Greek and Roman sources say between 70 and 300 languages were spoken in Dioscurias alone.
Sarduri II of Urartu recorded a victory over Qulḫa in the mid-8th century BCE, and Askold Ivanchik holds that Qulḫa flourished as an independent state in the second half of that century.
Under the Achaemenids the southern tribes formed the 19th satrapy while the northern tribes sent 100 girls and 100 boys to the Persian court every five years.
dyk: The oldest 'Colchian' coins, dated to the mid-6th century BCE and long the primary evidence for a Colchian state, have on reassessment turned out to be the production of an Achaemenid satrapy.
ev: Sarduri II, king of Urartu, inscribes his victory over Qulḫa on a stele.
second half of the 8th century BCE
Qulḫa flourishes as an independent state, by Askold Ivanchik's reading of cuneiform texts and archaeology, but hardly survives the end of the century.
Scythians and Cimmerians migrating from Central Asia invade Colchis; the Scythians make a base on the kingdom's former territory for raids into Media and Anatolia.
The kingdom of Colchis (Kolkheti) emerges in western Georgia, what Svante Cornell calls the beginning of proto-Georgian statehood.
The oldest 'Colchian' coins are struck, now understood as the output of an Achaemenid satrapy.
Shortly after reaching Trapezus, the Ten Thousand decisively defeat the Colchians in battle.

f.capital: No single seat is recorded; the chief towns were Phasis (Poti), Dioscurias (Sukhumi), Surium (Vani), Archaeopolis (Nokalakevi) and Cyta or Aia (Kutaisi)
f.predecessor: The Colchian Bronze Age culture of the eastern Black Sea; the Qulḫa of the Urartian inscriptions
f.successor: Pontus under Mithridates VI, who gave Colchis to his son in 83 BCE; then Roman dynasts and the kingdom of Lazica (Egrisi)
